candidate.answerReason: Squaring the successive radii produces areas π, π/4, π/16, …. This convergent geometric series has sum π/(1−1/4)=4π/3.

methods.label: Find the geometric series of areas
methods.explanation:
A circle's area is \(\pi r^2\), so halving the radius multiplies its area by \(\left(\frac12\right)^2=\frac14\). The areas are therefore
\[
\pi,\quad \frac{\pi}{4},\quad \frac{\pi}{16},\quad\ldots.
\]
An infinite geometric series with first term \(u\) and common ratio \(q\) has sum \(\frac{u}{1-q}\) when \(|q|<1\). Here \(u=\pi\) and \(q=\frac14\), so the convergence condition holds. The sum is
\[
\frac{\pi}{1-1/4}=\boxed{\frac{4\pi}{3}}
\]
square inches, choice D.
